{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -o job.%j.out
#   --partition=gpulab02
#   --qos=gpulab02
#   -J myFirstGPUJob
#   --job-name=Unet
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=6
#   --gres=gpu:1

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 6 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --queue=gpulab02 \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm %j output naming using Flux job id.
exec >"job.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

# NOTE: Slurm --qos=gpulab02 has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: QoS-related limits/priority/preemption behavior may not be applied, changing queue time
# or job survivability.

# NOTE: Slurm job names (-J myFirstGPUJob and --job-name=Unet) are not expressed here as portable Flux batch directives.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

nvidia-smi

python3 script_train.py --datadir ../datasets/cityscapes --batch_size 4 --num_gpu 1 --losstype segment
# python deeplabv2_resnet101_cityscapes/test_cuda.py
'
"
}
